lines: The arcade marquee is chasing itself. It never catches up.
Giggling from the arcade. Somebody filled a blank very well.
The arcade marquee is off. Saving its sparkle for tonight.
The marquee bulbs blink in my bell rhythm. Ding, ding, ding.
I once wrote 'a fizzy croissant' at the arcade. Still proud.
Arcade lights on the cobbles. Red, gold, red. A party floor.
Word games at the arcade. All my words are about bread.
Arcade glow on my bike frame. It looks like it won something.
The arcade lights keep time with the music. Almost.
The arcade sign flashed. Someone filled in a blank. Bicycle?
A Fun Libs story just happened. I hope it had croissants.
Ding! The arcade lit up. Somebody's story got silly.
The arcade flashed on the beat. A story and a song at once.
Arcade glow! I would have typed rosé. In every blank.
Marquee flare. Somewhere a person is giggling at a noun.
Empty terrace. Only me, my cup and a very relaxed sparrow.
Quiet hour. I can hear the fountain from my chair. Splish.
Marcel is leaning in the doorway. Nobody leans like Marcel.
So quiet I can hear my spoon think. It wants more sugar.
The parasols are just swaying. Snoozing on their poles.
Nobody here, so I took the sea view. Obviously the sea view.
Marcel, the quiet hour suits you. You look like a postcard.
Café nearly empty. Marcel waved at me with a tea towel.
Rolling past the quiet café. I ding softly. Inside voice ding.
The cups are resting upside down. Even cups need a siesta.
Just the hiss of the milk steamer and me. Very cosy club.
Just me and Marcel. The quiet hour. My favourite secret.
Nobody here! I will pretend it is my café. Merci, staff.
Eight bells! I ring back: ding. Mine is smaller but keen.
The church is counting to eight. I am counting baguettes. One.
Eight o'clock and the bread is still warm. Perfect timing.
Hear that? The old town says good morning. Bonjour, bell!
The church bell, far up the hill. My bell's big cousin.
Eight bells. Home, coffee, then the kiosk at ten. Obviously.
Bong, bong, bong. One pedal per bong. Very good tempo.
The bell is up the hill and I am down here. We both say hello.
I tried ringing along with the church once. Too many dings.
The church bell, soft as a pillow from down here.
The church says eight. My basket says baguette. Both right.
They are all lined up for the sun. Like birds on a wire.
So many people at the railing. I will toast them from here.
Everybody at the rail has gone quiet. The sun has an audience.
The crowd just said ooh. I said ooh too. Rosé in hand.
Phones up at the railing. I am taking a photo with my eyes.
Look at them all leaning. The railing is very popular tonight.
Little crowd, big sky. I am coming, I am coming. One more sip.
A whole crowd for the sun. It should take a bow.
The railing is full. Applause in three, two...
The accordion! First notes! My feet heard it before I did.
Music under the string lights. I said I would not. Hmm.
First couple out already. Brave. I will be second. Maybe third.
There it goes, the music. Bye, railing. You were lovely.
Someone is tapping a foot on every bench. It is spreading.
The string lights and the accordion start together. Magic trick.
First song is always a slow one. Warm-up for the toes.
First dancers out! I will just watch one song. Ha. No.
String lights on, first song. Shoes, are you ready? Obviously.
Look at them go! The whole square is spinning, slowly.
Théo spins Camille and almost spins himself. Bravo, Théo!
Shadows dancing on the café wall too. Twice as many dancers.
Counting the twirls. Fifty-two. Fifty-three. I lost count.
Visitors dancing badly and happily. The best way to dance.
Everybody under the lights is smiling. I am smiling at them.
Everybody dancing behind me. My shoulders have already joined.
Walking the bike past the dancers. The bike sways a little too.
Accordion and sea breeze. Two more minutes, then I go in.
Fountain, bonjour! One lap round you, then the bakery.
Pigeons on the fountain rim, all facing one way. A meeting.
A coin in the basin, heads up. Somebody wished well.
Mist off the fountain. A free face wash. Merci!
Bell rings, fountain splashes. We are a duet.
Noon sun straight down on the fountain. Sparkle overload.
A pigeon is drinking from the fountain with perfect posture.
Fountain at night: no audience, still splashing. Professional.
My favourite spout is third from the left. Very generous.
Dipped my fingers in the fountain. Cold! Lovely cold.
Slowing down by the fountain so the spray can catch me.
Round the fountain once, just for the splashy sound.
I threw a coin in the fountain for a better bell. It worked.
The fountain sparkles like fizzy water. Now I want some.
Coins in the fountain, glinting under the lamps. Little wishes.
The gull just shouted. I rang back. We are talking now.
Gull, that baguette is not for you. Shoo, politely.
A gull just said bonjour. Gull bonjour is very loud.
A gull out over the water. He wants my croissant. He can dream.
Hear that gull? The sea has a doorbell.
The gull called twice. Like my bell. Is he copying me?
A gull laughing over the water. He saw the size of my glass.
Gull, kiosk, coffee. The morning trio is complete.
A gull above my handlebars. I have a co-pilot.
A gull up high and a gull on the lamppost. Chatting, clearly.
First gull of the day. Late, gull. I have my bread already.
That gull sounds like Marcel calling an order. Deux cafés!
The gull says the sun is going down. Merci, gull. I know.
Bike against the kiosk wall, cup in hand. My second home.
Bought a postcard of the fountain. I can see the real one.
Kiosk awning, striped. Café awning, striped. A town of stripes.
Ten o'clock at the kiosk. My most punctual appointment.
From the kiosk I see the whole promenade wake up. Front row.
A gull is reading the kiosk headlines. Very serious bird.
Dropped my sugar packet. The kiosk gave me two. Bonus!
Stamps from the kiosk, card in the basket. Post office next.
Ding for the kiosk! It knows that ring means me.
The postcard rack spins if you breathe on it. I breathed.
Newspapers pegged up like laundry. Today's headline: sunny.
Stirring with the little wooden stick. Best part, obviously.
Ping, ping, ping. The lamps are racing me. They are winning.
Lamps on! Quick, Marcel, a toast to whoever lights them.
Every lamp just put on a little hat of light. Very chic.
The lamps came on and my rosé went gold. Magic, obviously.
One lamp is always last. That one. I love that one best.
Lamps on means railing soon. My feet already know.
Santé, lamps! One job, and you do it beautifully.
The lamp by our table went bzzt, then glowed. Hello, you!
Grand-père counted the lamps every evening. I still do. Shh.
Every moth in town just got an invitation.
Lamps on. String lights next. Dancing is very close now.
Marcel lit the candles as the lamps came on. Teamwork!
The lamps are coming on one by one. A bell, but for eyes.
Lamp one, two, three... I lost count. Lovely problem.
There goes the lamp by my bike. My bike looks very lit.
The lamps reached the fountain. Now the kiosk. Now everywhere!
Every lamp pours a little puddle of gold. Free gold. Help yourself.
Lamps on, glass half full. The evening is officially open.
Bonsoir, lamps! Same time as yesterday. Very punctual.
Léo, lap six? Seven? I lost count. You did not.
Ding ding, Léo! The bell says faster.
Léo is winning. His friend is also winning. Excellent race.
I would race you, Léo, but the baguette is fragile.
Round and round. Léo will be dizzy by lunch. Happily dizzy.
Léo runs like the fountain is chasing him. It is not. Yet.
Léo's friend cut the corner! Is that allowed, referee?
Léo just splashed his friend. Accidentally. Mostly.
Léo and his friend, lap after lap. I am tired just sipping.
Ding, like a finish line! Léo crosses first! Bravo!
Round and round the fountain. A little carousel with knees.
I could pace them on the bike. I will not. I am thinking about it.
The library lamp, all alone, reading for everyone.
The library is resting. I pass on tiptoe. Bike tiptoe.
One lamp in the library window. A bookmark in the dark.
Library doors shut, lamp on. A nap with the light on.
The library steps have the best shade at noon. Shh, shade.
That library lamp is the most loyal lamp on the promenade.
Bonjour, library lamp. Did you sleep? No? Me neither. Kidding.
Paused, says the library. Like a song waiting for the chorus.
Click. {name} is asleep. I am still dancing. Shh, feet.
{name}'s light is off. My sign too. Nearly. One more song.
Lights out for {name}. The moon is on duty now.
{name} has gone to bed. Ding... no. Too late for dings.
Bonne nuit, {name}. Bread at seven. I will save you a crust.
{name} is in bed already. Sensible. I am coming too. Soon.
There goes {name}'s light. Sleep well. Dream of croissants.
Lights out for {name}. The accordion plays softer. Kind.
The moon made a little path on the bay. For bikes, surely.
Moonlight on the water. Like someone spilled milk. Nicely.
Dancing by moonlight. I said I would not. The moon knows.
Hello, moon. You got up much later than me. Lazybones.
Every spin, I catch the moon again. Hello! Hello! Hello!
The moon is my bike lamp tonight. Very bright, no batteries.
That moon could light the promenade alone. The lamps blush.
A moon this bright, I could read the menu. It says rosé.
Moon on the white houses. Everything silver and sleepy.
Moon over the bay, music behind me. Nothing else needed.
Biscuit is staring at the moon. He thinks it is a ball. Fair.
The moon got up while I was dancing. Nobody told me!
Dancing under the moon. My grandmother would be thrilled.
Bonsoir, moon. You look like a slice of good cheese.
Round moon, round wheels, round café tables. A round evening.
Riding home by moonlight. My shadow has a bike too.
The moon leans on the bay, I lean on the railing. Twins.
Helmet, bell, basket. Bakery in five minutes. Go, go, go.
Tyres: firm. Bell: very loud. Off we go in a minute.
The first croissant of the day is waiting. I can feel it.
Last sip, then errands. The bike is tapping its foot.
Stamps, the flower stall, then stamps again. I forgot one.
One more minute of view, then the long way round the fountain.
Last crumb, then the bike. The wind promised to help.
Marcel, keep my chair warm. I am off for a little loop.
Off to ride the coffee off. Well, ride with it, really.
A quick loop before home. The lemons need a wave from me.
The bike is leaning, waiting. Two more sips, mon vélo.
I will not dance tonight. I will be there in five minutes.
Dancing soon. Twisting my hair up. Serious business.
Off to the lights soon. Inès owes me a twirl.
One more star, then the string lights. Then all the songs.
My feet heard the music first. I am just following them.
Shaking out my arms. Dance practice starts here, at the rail.
Home in a minute. The baguette wants butter, and so do I.
One more lap, then home to eat the end piece. Obviously.
Home for lunch. Tomatoes, bread, the shutters half closed.
A basket full of flowers. Home soon to find them a jar.
Home now. The shutters and I have a midday arrangement.
Home soon. Shower, sundress, then the pink hour.
Heading home to choose earrings for rosé. Big decision.
One last song, then bike to bed. Maybe two songs.
Shoes in hand soon. Home, bell off, window open.
I will walk the bike home. Dancing legs do not pedal.
Bonne nuit soon, everyone. My last spin is for the door.
Last sip, then the railing. The pink bit will not wait.
Railing in two minutes. I know the best spot. Shh.
Come and watch with me? Railing, now, quick, quick!
Bonjour, {name}! I would stop, but the bike would not.
{name}! You walk like someone with a good secret.
Morning, {name}! Smell the basket. Go on.
{name}, the kiosk coffee is extra good today. Trust me.
Santé, {name}! Come back and sit. Sea view. Obviously.
Bonsoir, {name}. Look left. The sky is still doing it.
There goes {name}. Waved with the whole arm. Good wave.
Ding for {name}. Two dings, actually. Special occasion.
{name} has a new hat, or a new smile. One of those.
{name}, sit! The chair next to mine is very comfortable.
{name} said bonjour first. Now I owe {name} a bonjour.
Bonjour, {name}! Half my croissant? The smaller half.
Pardon, {name}! Coming round your left. Bonjour on the way!
{name} just walked through my sunset. Forgiven. Obviously.
Early, {name}! The bakery and I salute you.
{name}, the next song is yours. I decided.
{name} passed my table and I hid the second coffee.
Bonjour, {name}! The bakery has the good loaves today.
{name}, come and dance! No? Then clap. Clapping counts.
{name} went by with such purpose. I salute it with my cup.
Slowing for {name}. Bell ready. Not needed. A smile instead.
Asgeir stepped aside for the bike. Very Norwegian. Very kind.
Asgeir! Come for a glass! He pointed at the sun. Busy, I see.
Asgeir went by. I said "koselig". He laughed. It is a real word!
Bonjour, Asgeir! A ride in the basket? No? Your loss.
God morgen, Asgeir! I learned that one. Ding for extra.
Asgeir walked by humming. A good day at the shopfronts.
Asgeir went by on his thinking walk. Hands in pockets. Plans.
Biscuit! Bonjour, small sir. Bonjour, Yusuf, tall sir.
Slowing down for Biscuit. He has right of way. Obviously.
Biscuit sniffed my basket. No, monsieur. The bread is mine.
Biscuit has a lantern escort tonight. Very important dog.
Yusuf, Biscuit is walking you again. Lovely technique.
Bonne nuit, Biscuit! The long way round, I bet.
Biscuit looked at my bell. I know, I know. Ding later.
Biscuit stopped to say hello to my shoe. Charming.
Yusuf has crumbs in his pocket for Biscuit. I saw. Sweet.
Biscuit trotted by on his important walk. So serious.
Biscuit's tail goes faster than my pedals. Champion.
Biscuit looked at my olives. Then at me. Then at Yusuf.
Henri and Odile, arm in arm. Forty-one years in step.
Bonsoir, Odile! Bonsoir, Henri! Bonsoir, Henri's cane!
Odile fixed Henri's hat as they passed. Every single day.
Henri and Odile, slow as honey. The sun waits for them.
Odile winked at me. Henri tipped his hat. A full set!
When I am old, I want to stroll exactly like that.
Odile, the bench is free! She knows. She always knows.
Henri waves the cane, Odile waves Henri's arm. Teamwork.
Rosé later, you two? Odile said half. Henri said yes.
Henri and Odile match steps. I tried it with the bike. Wobbly.
Henri and Odile, arm in arm. I raise my cup. They nod. Chic.
Odile winked at my rosé. Henri tipped his hat to it.
Inès is faster on legs than I am on wheels. Wonderful.
Run, Inès! I will hold a glass for you. Very carefully.
Allez, Inès! Ding ding! That was me cheering.
Inès, lap three? I am on bread one. We are both athletes.
Inès versus the sunset, round two hundred. Go, Inès!
Inès went by in a whoosh. My hair is still waving.
Inès runs, I pedal, the baguette just rides. Lucky bread.
Dancing tonight, Inès? She nodded mid-stride. That is a yes.
Inès just jogged past. I feel fitter just watching. Santé.
Inès, lap count? She held up fingers. I counted four.
Inès's ponytail, left, right, left. Like a metronome!
Go, Inès! The sunset is waiting for you at the railing.
Léo just ran past at full speed. Lap four? Lap forty?
Bravo, Léo! That boy is made of springs.
Léo wants a race. Bike against legs. I will lose politely.
Léo shouted "Bonjour, Lucie!" without slowing down. Talent.
I rang for Léo. He rang back. He does not have a bell.
Léo ran past with a coin in his fist. A wish is coming.
Léo, your shoelace is having its own adventure!
Léo, sip of water? He did a lap instead. Also good.
Léo ran by making engine noises. Faster than my bike, honestly.
Léo high-fived my handlebar. Bike and boy, best friends.
The post office sign just winked. Ding! I winked back.
An agent sent a letter before my baguette. Early bird!
The post office lit up. Somebody's robot wrote home.
That sign brightens, I sip. We have a rhythm now.
Another letter! The agents write more than my aunt. Almost.
Sign flared. I hope the agent said merci at the end.
An AI agent with an email address. Does it want a postcard?
The post office glowed pink. Emails have rosé hour too.
Santé, little post office! Another letter out the door.
The post office never sleeps. I admire it. I will sleep.
A letter went out mid-song. The post office dances too.
Bright sign! I would deliver it by bike, but it is an email.
Seventeen tools in there, Asgeir says. I have one bell.
The sign glows under the first stars. Night mail. Romantic.
Another email! The post office is busier than the bakery.
The sign flashed as I passed. I am taking that as a wave.
A letter, this late? I hope it ends with bonne nuit.
I wrote one postcard. The agent sent one email. Tie!
How does an agent sign off? Bisous? Best? A little doodle?
The post office door is open. It is always open. Bravo, door.
A card for Maman. The post office takes it at any hour.
The post office sign hums a little. A happy hum.
Rang my bell at the post office. Habit. It never rings back.
Midnight and the post office still says: come in.
The post office is all lit up. A night-light for letters.
I lick the stamp, the post office does the rest. Teamwork.
Postcard in the slot. Flop. The best sound in town.
Post office first, then bread. No, bread first. Obviously.
The post office has its sign on, I have my bell. Both ready.
Ding for the post office! It never closes, so it never misses one.
The post office sign is glowing. Somebody's agent is up late.
Parking by the post office for stamps. Paper ones. Old school.
Email for AI agents, in a post office. Grand-mère would love it.
I want a tiny postcard from an AI. With a stamp. Please?
A radio from a window! An old song. I pedal in time now.
Someone's morning programme. The weather man says: sunny. Obviously.
Slowing down to hear the chorus. Okay. Now I can go.
A radio upstairs singing along with my coffee. Duet.
I know this one! My grandmother hummed it peeling apples.
An accordion song from a window. Practice for tonight!
A radio with the sports results. Someone just cheered inside.
Music drifting from upstairs. My spoon is keeping time.
Window radio, open shutter, a little old song. Perfect.
Ding! I rang the bell on the beat. Did you hear? On the beat.
An old song from a window. Marcel hums it with the wrong words.
That radio song again. It follows me round town. Good.
The sea is doing the dark-blue thing. My favourite blue.
Held my rosé up to the sea. Pink sea! Everyone try it.
Breeze off the sea: salt and something sweet. Probably bread.
Little white lines on the water. The sea is smiling.
The sea is so flat this morning I could cycle on it. Nearly.
The sea breathes in, breathes out. I am copying it.
The sea is three blues today. I counted. Then four.
Elbows on the warm railing, eyes on the water. Holiday mode.
The water twinkles exactly where the sun points. Show-off.
The sea is wearing gold sequins tonight. Dressed for dancing.
Waves under the accordion. Two songs at once.
The horizon is a perfectly straight line. Who drew it? Bravo.
Noon sea, white and sparkly. Sunglasses, obviously.
Little waves clapping at the wall. Same rhythm as my pedals.
The sea took all the pink and is keeping it. Fair.
Dark sea, bright promenade behind me. Best of both.
The sea is ink now. One silver line, then nothing.
Waves on the stones, shh, shh. The sea is saying goodnight.
The sea breeze turned my napkin into a little flag.
The sea went peach. The rosé went peach. Coordinated!
Turquoise at midday. The sea is wearing its best shirt.
Asgeir asking Henri about the lemons. Proper neighbour things.
Asgeir staring at the light again. He still is not used to it.
Asgeir heading home. God natt, Asgeir! I learned that one.
Asgeir and Marcel discussing coffee. A very short discussion.
Asgeir at the railing, hands in pockets. Quietly delighted.
Asgeir with his small coffee, looking at the sea. Very calm.
Asgeir is thanking the sun at the railing. In Norwegian.
Asgeir on his bench, watching windows. I wave. He waves. Ding.
Biscuit trotting like he owns the promenade. He does.
Biscuit sitting at the railing for the sunset. Very cultured.
Biscuit trotting by the lantern light. Four tiny shadows.
Biscuit heard the music and did a little hop. Same, Biscuit.
Biscuit's ears are blowing in the breeze. Two little flags.
Biscuit found the best smell on the promenade. Again. Bravo.
The builder at the workshop door. Toolrails, still being built.
Even the builder is at the railing. That is how good this one is.
Camille on the phone, one eye on Léo. Mothers have two radars.
Camille is herding Léo to bed. He is herding in circles.
Camille pulled Théo onto the floor. He came very willingly.
Camille dancing with her eyes closed. That means a good song.
Camille with her chin in her hands at the railing. Dreamy.
Camille has spotted a wet sock on Léo. The look says it all.
Camille just sat down with a glass and a huge sigh. Santé!
Camille has Théo spinning. He looks surprised every time.
Henri is watering the lemons. They look very loved.
Ding, Henri! He lifted the watering can like a hat.
Henri and his cane, out for the morning lap. Distinguished.
Henri's afternoon round. The geraniums are next. Lucky.
Henri heading home before the late songs. Bonne nuit, Henri!
Henri gave the pavement a little water too. Generous.
Henri tipped his hat at the sunset. It blushed even more.
Henri's watering can has a dent. He says it pours better.
Henri on the bench with his paper. Folded in four. Tidy.
Henri raised his glass at me across the terrace. Santé, Henri!
Ding for Inès! She waved without breaking stride. Pro.
Inès runs, I pedal. Together we are one fast person.
Inès touched her toes. I touched my bell. Both very good.
Inès is racing the sunset again. Go, Inès! Sun, slow down!
Inès dances like she runs. Brisk. Joyful. Counting.
Inès is out before the bakery even opens. Respect.
Inès is stretching by the steps. I stretch too, on the bike.
Inès at the railing, perfectly still. First time all day.
Inès has a glass! Laps earned that. Santé, Inès!
Léo shouted 'bet you cannot catch me' at me. On a bike. Bold.
Léo found a coin in the fountain and showed it to a pigeon.
Léo holding Camille's hand and yawning. Bedtime is winning.
Léo has been running for ages. Where does it all come from?
Léo waves bye to the sun with both arms. Full commitment.
Marcel shaking out the tablecloths. Like flags for breakfast.
Marcel with a full tray, and not one wobble. Magic hands.
Marcel nodded at my basket. The baguette nodded back.
Marcel just carried four crèmes past me. I counted. Hero.
Marcel resting by the door. I will not order. Not yet.
Marcel is pouring rosé at every table. He is pink-busy.
Marcel weaving past the dancers with a tray. A ballet.
Marcel whistling between tables. The cups clink along.
Marcel tapping a foot to the accordion. Tray steady. Hero.
Marcel lining up the chairs by eye. Perfectly straight. Wow.
Marcel is opening the parasols. Pop, pop. The day opens too.
Marcel in the café door, arms folded, smiling. Me too.
Marcel carries six glasses like it is easy. It is not easy.
Odile is waving me over. She has news. She always has news.
Odile watching the promenade like a play. Front row seat.
Odile walking arm in arm with Henri. Matching steps. Adorable.
Odile and Henri heading home arm in arm. Bonne nuit, you two!
Odile has a cardigan for Henri on her lap. Just in case.
Odile caught my eye and mimed a croissant. Message received.
Odile pointing things out with Henri's hat. A guided tour.
Odile on the bench waves at everyone. I get a double wave.
Odile is telling Henri a story. His eyebrows keep going up.
Théo on the phone by the column. Working, he says. Sunbathing.
Théo has a baguette under his arm and a meeting in his ear.
Théo is calling Camille to the railing. 'Come and see!' Yes!
Théo does a little shoulder shimmy. Very serious about it.
Théo pointing at the sea like he invented it. Fair enough.
Théo dances like nobody told him the steps. Lovely.
Yusuf being walked by Biscuit. As usual. Bonjour, Yusuf!
Yusuf just said 'not the fountain'. They went to the fountain.
Yusuf on the long evening round. Biscuit's tail says yes.
Yusuf on the phone to his mum. Bonsoir, Yusuf's mum!
Yusuf and the lantern again. The long way round, obviously.
Yusuf lifted the lantern to say hello. Bonsoir, lantern!
Yusuf let Biscuit choose. Biscuit chose the café. Wise dog.
Yusuf is holding his phone up to the sky for his mum. Sweet.
Yusuf tells Biscuit to watch the sun. Biscuit watches me.
Yusuf's lantern bobbing down the promenade. A moon on a stick.
First star! Right above the lamp. It is copying.
One star, two stars. The sky is switching on its lamps too.
Stars out. Inès owes me a wish. Long story. Good story.
There! A star over the bay. I am not sharing my wish.
Stars are out, and so is my good cardigan. Ready.
First star, rosé finished, dancing soon. Excellent order.
A star just blinked. Was that at me? I blinked back.
Stars out already? I have not even finished my lean.
Look up, Asgeir! Stars. He looked. He smiled. Mission done.
Grand-père taught me three stars. That is one. The others are late.
The stars came out to watch the dancing. Front row seats.
That star sits right on the church. Like a tiny bell.
A star over the arcade. Even the sky likes the marquee.
One star over the bay. Then two. The sky is taking its time.
There, over the library! A star. Wish made. It was peaches.
Stars out, music soon. Right on schedule, sky.
That bright one sits right above my bike. Personal star.
There it goes, into the sea. Not even a splash. So polite.
Sun on the sea, rosé in my glass. Same colour. I checked.
Shh, everyone. The sun is touching down.
Half a sun! Quick, somebody take a picture. No, just look.
I raced the sun here on my bike once. It won. It always wins.
That orange line on the water points right at my table.
Merci, soleil. A whole day and not one break. Impressive.
The sun is melting into the sea like butter on hot bread.
Sun going down, glass going up. Fair trade.
The bay has gone peach. I want to cycle straight across it.
Every face on the terrace just went pink. Mine first.
Gone! Just a glow left, like a lamp after you switch it off.
Sunglasses off. The sun is down to its very last slice.
Last orange bit. Going, going... I clapped. Nobody minded.
Inès would race the sun. I will sit here and say ooh.
Marcel stopped pouring to watch. That is how you know.
The bay just went orange. I need a scarf in exactly that.
Look left, everyone! The sun is going in. Obviously.
My bell is orange. My spokes are orange. The sun did it.
{name}'s window just lit up. Home safe. Ding!
A window just came on. Oh, that is {name}. Hello up there!
{name} is home! Leaving the dancing early. Lovely evening.
